source.check: returned unopposed: named for the division in the Returning Officer's notice of result, no poll being taken (Irish News, 10 June 1964)

note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Saintfield was the only division contested: Herbert Rogers polled 1,903 and John Johnston 924, so Rogers was returned and Johnston was not. The other eighteen divisions were filled without a contest. The Returning Officer's 'Notice of Result of Elections 1964 - County of Down', dated 4 June 1964 and printed in the Irish News of 10 June 1964, p. 2, names the person returned for every division except Newry: the Newry Urban poll had been countermanded because Mr. F. G. Mulligan (Newry Labour) died between nomination day and polling day, and the Irish News of 13 June 1964 reports that Newry Labour then decided not to renominate anyone, so the seat was left unfilled and no return is made for it. The notice prints no party labels, so none are recorded. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
